title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZN (Amalgamation, merger or division, etc., to form new Producer Company)

content.overview: Section 378ZN permits Producer Companies to adopt specified resolutions to transfer assets and liabilities, divide, amalgamate or merge, subject to member approval and statutory safeguards for Members and creditors. The operative text specifies a two-thirds threshold among Members present and voting, notice to Members and creditors, a one-month option for non-consenting Members or creditors, and required particulars in the resolution.
content.glance: Section 378ZN governs resolutions for asset/liability transfer, division, amalgamation or merger of Producer Companies, with member-voting, notice, dissenting-member/creditor and resolution-content safeguards.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZN (Amalgamation, merger or division, etc., to form new Producer Companies). The section permits a Producer Company to resolve to transfer all or part of its assets and liabilities to another Producer Company for section 378B objects, or divide itself into two or more new Producer Companies. Two or more Producer Companies may resolve to amalgamate into a new Producer Company or merge one into another. The resolutions require the majority specified by subsection (3): a majority of total Members with voting rights, not less than two-thirds of Members present and voting. The section also requires written notice with the proposed resolution to Members and creditors; provides a one-month option for non-consenting Members to transfer shares with Board approval to an active Member and for non-consenting creditors to withdraw deposits, loans or advances; deems failure to exercise the option within that period consent; and delays the resolution's effect until one month expires or all Members and creditors assent, whichever is earlier. The resolution must include the matters listed in subsection (8). This update is limited to the reviewed statutory text; remaining sub-sections and full current-law verification remain open.

sections.heading: Available resolutions
sections.body: A Producer Company may resolve to transfer all or part of its assets and liabilities to another Producer Company, which agrees by resolution, for objects specified in section 378B; or divide itself into two or more new Producer Companies. Two or more Producer Companies may resolve to amalgamate and form a new Producer Company or merge one into another.

sections.heading: Member approval threshold
sections.body: Every resolution under the section must be passed at a general meeting by a majority of total Members having voting rights, not less than two-thirds of the Members present and voting. The resolution must contain particulars of the transfer, division, amalgamation or merger, as applicable.

sections.heading: Notice and non-consenting parties
sections.body: Before passing the resolution, the Producer Company must give written notice and a copy of the proposed resolution to all Members and creditors, who may give consent. A Member or creditor who does not consent has, during one month from service of notice, the option specified in subsection (5): a Member may transfer shares with Board approval to an active Member and cease to be a Member; a creditor may withdraw the deposit, loan or advance. Failure to exercise the option within that period is deemed consent.

sections.heading: When the resolution takes effect and required contents
sections.body: The resolution does not take effect until one month expires or all Members and creditors have assented, whichever is earlier. Subsection (8) requires the resolution to provide for the future conduct of the company's affairs, purchase of Members' shares or interests, consequent share-capital reduction where relevant, and specified treatment of agreements with directors, secretaries and managers. The remaining statutory provisions must be checked against the full current text before relying on the topic as a complete statement of section 378ZN.

distinctions.left: Section 378ZN distinguishes transfer of assets/liabilities to another Producer Company and division into two or more new Producer Companies.
distinctions.right: It separately permits two or more Producer Companies to amalgamate into a new Producer Company or merge one into another.

misconceptions.trap: Treating member approval alone as the whole statutory process.
misconceptions.correction: Check notice to Members and creditors, the options for non-consenting parties, the effective-date rule and required resolution particulars.

misconceptions.trap: Applying a generic majority threshold without the section's stated voting test.
misconceptions.correction: Use the threshold in subsection (3): a majority of total Members with voting rights, not less than two-thirds of Members present and voting.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a resolution takes effect immediately when passed.
misconceptions.correction: Apply subsection (7)'s timing rule and check whether all Members and creditors have assented.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 378zn do?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Two or more Producer Companies may amalgamate, merge or divide by the procedure in the section, with the approval of the members and the Registrar.
